subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 25-year-old man undergoes a maximal exercise test as part of a physiology study. During exercise his skeletal muscle oxygen consumption increases several-fold, mixed venous oxygen content falls, and blood lactate rises from 1.2 to 3.0 mmol/L. Muscle ADP concentration rises while ATP remains relatively constant.
question: Which of the following best explains the increase in mitochondrial oxygen consumption?

options.text: ADP availability stimulates electron transport and oxidative phosphorylation
Protons are pumped into the mitochondrial matrix
The proton gradient across the inner mitochondrial membrane is eliminated
FADH2 replaces NADH as the only electron donor

explanation_correct: Mitochondrial respiration is tightly coupled to ATP demand: when ATP is used and ADP rises, ATP synthase accelerates proton re-entry into the matrix, which increases electron transport and oxygen consumption. This respiratory control allows ATP production to match cellular demand during exercise.

explanation_incorrect.B: ATP inhibits, rather than stimulates, electron transport; it is the ADP level that rises during exercise.
explanation_incorrect.C: Electron transport pumps protons from the matrix into the intermembrane space, not into the matrix.
explanation_incorrect.D: The proton gradient is maintained and used; its elimination would indicate uncoupling, which would not efficiently produce ATP.
explanation_incorrect.E: NADH remains a major electron donor; FADH2 contributes but does not replace NADH.

educationalObjective: Oxidative phosphorylation is regulated by ADP availability, so increased ATP turnover during exercise raises mitochondrial oxygen consumption.
